Header: 2026-05-19 11:30 PT | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Ethan Park (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (Head of Platform, Polaris); Markus Rey (SRE); Sofia Kim (Security)

Summary (auto): discovery call to understand Polaris Tech's integration needs across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments. Focus on SDK support (python/node), LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits and quota policies, observability hooks and security requirements (SSO, KMS, VPC).

Topics: Integration points, onboarding effort, security/compliance, perf benchmarks, next steps/POC

Transcript:
00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya with Redwood Inference, our AE, and with me is Ethan Park, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:06 Lena: Good morning, thanks for organizing, we've been evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a while so keen to understand the integration story.
00:12 Ethan: Awesome. Quick agenda: we'll ask about current stack, show how the SDKs and langchain examples look, talk about gateway/proxy patterns you mentioned in the RFP, and then security/observability.
00:20 Markus: Sounds good. Just to set context, we're running a python microservice that uses LangChane and Llama Index, we also have a Node backend for realtime chat. Right now we're self-hosting a model for chat but costs and ops are getting heavy.
00:35 Maya: Got it, that matches what you sent. Can you tell us more about volumes and SLOs?
00:40 Lena: We're a payments platform, so bursts during peak processing windows, 2000 concurrent chat sessions is a rough max, long tail latency we care about is p99 under 600ms for short prompts.
00:52 Ethan: Ok, big picture: Hosted API is easiest to start, Dedicated gives predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools, Private/VPC is for when you need customer-managed networking and on-prem. For integration, SDKs are first-class: python and node, plus official connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex.
01:08 Markus: On the LangChain bit, what's the effort? We have a lot of custom chains and prompt templates.
01:13 Ethan: Usually small. Our SDK exposes an OpenAI-compatible surface but also adds streaming, function calls, and structured outputs. We maintain example repos: langchain-redwood-python, llamaindex-redwood, and a node chat quickstart. For custom chains you mostly swap provider client and tweak tokenization config. We'll send the quickstart.
01:27 Lena: And for the KV cache/prefix caching, we use a cached embedding + retrieval flow, any special hooks?
01:33 Ethan: Yes, we have automatic KV cache support in the runtime and prefix caching options; the SDK exposes cache controls and ability to pin cache keys to sessions. For retrieval-heavy workloads we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching plus batching.
01:45 Sofia: Security: we need SSO, RBAC, KMS for keys, audit logs, and SOC2. Do you support customer-managed keys?
01:52 Maya: Yes, for Dedicated and Private you can integrate with your KMS/HSM. Hosted supports envelope encryption and we have integrations with major KMS providers; for Dedicated we can do customer-managed keys. SOC2 and security questionnaire we'll share after the call.
02:05 Markus: Network path — we run in a VPC and have strict egress rules. If we go Dedicated or Private how does traffic route?
02:12 Ethan: Two options: 1) Redwood-hosted endpoints with VPC peering + private link-ish setup for Dedicated; 2) Private deployment within your VPC or on-prem package that keeps the control plane separated. For gateway/proxy patterns you mentioned, some customers run a lightweight request gateway in front of Redwood for auth, rate-limiting, and routing to Hosted or Dedicated backends.
02:31 Lena: We were curious about self-hosted gateway vs using Redwood's gateway. Do you offer a managed gateway?
02:36 Maya: We offer an optional managed gateway for enterprises, but many customers prefer a small proxy component (we provide a reference proxy) that handles auth and can do token transformation and per-route quotas before calling Redwood.
02:47 Markus: Speaking of quotas, how granular are rate limits? Can we have per-customer, per-route, per-model quotas?
02:54 Ethan: Yes. We support per-route and per-api-key quotas, RBAC controls, and can enforce rate limits at the tenant or route level. For Dedicated we can also enforce capacity reservations so you don't hit noisy-neighbor limits.
03:06 Lena: Observability — we need traces correlated with our tracing system and token-level cost breakdowns. What hooks exist?
03:12 Ethan: We provide tracing headers you can propagate (trace-id), structured response metadata with token counts, and webhooks for async events. The console has per-route latency and token-level cost views, plus logs and export APIs for S3 or our SIEM integration.
03:25 Sofia: How does logging work with PII-sensitive data? We can't log raw user content to a third party.
03:30 Maya: For Hosted we have configurable data retention and redaction options; for Dedicated/Private you can disable request logging or route logs to your own logging endpoint. We also support field-level redaction on ingest.
03:43 Markus: For the POC we'd like to run a throughput test and a tail-latency test with our typical prompt shapes. What's the recommended harness?
03:49 Ethan: We usually provide a synthetic harness that replays your request distributions, with options to test different sequence lengths. We'll include batching and kv cache toggles. For Dedicated, we'll suggest GPU types and quantization profiles for cost/latency tradeoffs.
04:05 Lena: Any gotchas with LangChain / LlamaIndex sessions and streaming? We have streaming chat and function calling.
04:11 Ethan: Streaming works fine; we support incremental tokens and delta events. Function calling is supported via structured outputs and we have examples that show how to integrate with LangChain agents. Note some third-party libraries have slight mismatch in callback interfaces — we'll include glue code.
04:24 Markus: Cost model — how do you bill? Per-token + optional reserved capacity?
04:28 Maya: Correct. Hosted is per-token; Dedicated can be reserved capacity plus usage-based adjustments for bursting. We'll include example math for your expected volumes.
04:35 Lena: What about on-prem? We have regulatory constraints in EU and APAC; could do a private deploy. How long to stand up?
04:42 Ethan: For Private on-prem it's a multi-week engagement — depends on hardware and network. VPC-hosted private deployments are quicker. We'll scope timeline in the POC planning.
04:51 Sofia: Can we run a security review and get SOC2 docs? Also do you support SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning?
04:58 Maya: Yes to both SAML and SCIM. We'll attach our SOC2 report and answers to your questionnaire. For Dedicated you get audit logs and longer retention options.
05:08 Lena: Any mention of competitors? We looked at Anthropic for chat, OpenAI for dev ergonomics. Curious on latency/price tradeoffs.
05:15 Maya: Anthropic and OpenAI are common comparisons; Redwood focuses on serving and predictability, especially for heavy throughput and deployed private workloads. We'll include comparative notes but we don't publish their pricing.
05:26 Markus: Small nit: some internal teams use Llama Index v0.6 and others LlamaIndex; watch for naming in docs.
05:33 Ethan: Noted, we'll include examples across versions.
05:36 Lena: Ok let's recap next steps.
05:40 Maya: Recap: we'll send pricing + SLA + SOC2 + KMS notes, SE will share benchmark harness and schedule a POC deep dive next week. We'll provide langchain/llamaindex quickstart repos. Customer will send compliance matrix and any hard network constraints.
05:54 Markus: Sounds good.
05:56 Sofia: Thanks, talk soon.
06:00 Maya: Thanks everyone.
